# Monaco's theme awareness reads a config that is null by design

## Context

Reported by @tobiu against the local portal in dark mode: every Monaco source pane renders with the light `vs` theme while the page around it is dark. Reproduced at `dev@87e3786673` on `/learn/benefits/body/FormsEngine`.

This is a regression of #8845 (*Sync Monaco Editor Theme in Portal*, closed), under epic #8727 (*Portal App Dark Theme*, closed).

## The Problem

Measured on three live editor instances via the Neural Link, on a page whose `document.body` carries `neo-theme-neo-dark`:

| property | value |
|---|---|
| `theme` (the config) | **`null`** |
| `getTheme()` | **`'neo-theme-neo-dark'`** |
| `editorTheme` | `'vs'` |
| `useThemeAwareness` | `true` |
| `mounted` | `true` |

DOM confirms it: all three `.monaco-editor` nodes carry class `vs` with `background-color: rgb(255, 255, 254)`.

**The resolved theme is correct and available. The component simply never asks for it.**

`src/component/wrapper/MonacoEditor.mjs:339`:

```js
afterSetTheme(value, oldValue) {
    if (this.useThemeAwareness && value) {
        this.editorTheme = value.includes('dark') ? 'vs-dark' : 'vs'
    }
}
```

It gates on the **raw `theme` config**, which is `theme_: null` by default (`component/Base.mjs:269`). For a component that *inherits* its theme rather than declaring one, that config stays `null` — so the hook never fires with a value and `editorTheme` keeps its `'vs'` default. `afterSetUseThemeAwareness` (`:311`) has the same defect: it re-invokes `afterSetTheme(this.theme, null)`, passing the same `null`.

**And `null` there is intentional, not an accident to repair upstream.** #18111's own docblock on `getTheme()` says so: *"a child inside a themed scope carries no theme class of its own by design"*. `getTheme()` (`component/Base.mjs:1522`) is the accessor that answers the real question by walking the component chain. Monaco's theme awareness predates that accessor and was never migrated to it.

Nothing supplies the config from outside either: `src/code/LivePreview.mjs:92` creates the editor with `module` / `header` / `hideLabel` / `listeners` / `style` / `reference` and no `theme`.

## The Architectural Reality

**The idiom already exists in the file that hosts this editor.** `src/code/LivePreview.mjs:486` reaches for exactly the right accessor when it themes the detached preview app:

```js
theme = me.getTheme?.();
// We overrule the viewport theme on purpose
if (theme) {
    mainView.theme = theme
}
```

So `LivePreview` asks `getTheme()` for the *preview* and the `MonacoEditor` beside it asks a null config for *itself*.

**The delivery path is intact — proven, not assumed.** Setting `editorTheme: 'vs-dark'` on one live instance turned **all three** editors dark (`rgb(30, 30, 30)`). Worth recording for whoever implements this: `main/addon/MonacoEditor.mjs:181` calls `monaco.editor.setTheme()`, which is **global** to the page rather than per-editor — `this.map[data.id] &&` is a created-yet gate, not a scoping mechanism. So the addon, the remote and the DOM all work; only the trigger is wrong.

**Two timing hazards a fix must not reintroduce.** `getInitialOptions()` passes `theme: me.editorTheme` at creation (`:450`), and `ffd860b664` (#18355) removed a `me.timeout(150)` that used to sit before `createInstance`. A repair that only corrects `afterSetTheme` still has to be right at creation, or it depends on a delay that no longer exists.

## The Fix

Resolve through `getTheme()` rather than the raw config, at both the hook and the creation site:

1. `afterSetTheme` and `afterSetUseThemeAwareness` consult `getTheme()` — the accessor that answers for an inheriting child.
2. `getInitialOptions()` builds its `theme` from the same resolution, so the editor is created correct rather than corrected afterwards.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1** In the dark portal, every `.monaco-editor` node carries `vs-dark`. Asserted on the **rendered node**, not on `editorTheme` — the config was never the thing the reader sees.
- **AC-2** ⚠️ **Both directions witnessed.** Light portal → `vs`, dark portal → `vs-dark`. An arm that only checks dark passes on a component hardcoded to `vs-dark`, which is the mirror of the bug being fixed.
- **AC-3** Correct **at creation**, not merely corrected after. `getInitialOptions()` must carry the resolved theme, since #18355 removed the delay a post-hoc correction used to hide behind.
- **AC-4** `useThemeAwareness: false` still opts out entirely, and an explicitly configured `theme` still wins over the inherited one.
- **AC-5** A theme **switch** while editors are mounted still repaints them. The portal has a live toggle, and this is the path #8845 originally shipped.

## Out of Scope

`component/Base.mjs#getTheme()` and theme propagation generally — the resolver is correct and returns the right answer here; this is a consumer that does not call it. Any other `useThemeAwareness` consumer (none found in `src/` or `apps/`). Mermaid's loader collision with Monaco (#18568) — same addon, unrelated defect.

## Avoided Traps

Do not "fix" this by propagating `theme` down to every child so the config stops being null. #18111 records the null as deliberate, and forcing a theme class onto children is the behaviour that ticket removed.

Do not reintroduce a delay before `createInstance` to let the theme arrive. #18355 removed that `timeout(150)` on purpose and a fix that depends on ordering luck will regress the same way.

Do not assert `editorTheme` and call it covered. It was `'vs'` here and the DOM agreed, but the reverse — a correct config that never reaches the DOM — is exactly the shape the addon's `map[data.id] &&` guard can produce silently.

## Related

- #8845 — the sync this regresses; #8727 the epic it shipped under.
- #18111 / #18106 — `getTheme()` walks components, and records the null-by-design contract.
- #18355 / `ffd860b664` — removed the pre-`createInstance` delay; relevant to AC-3.
- #18568 — Monaco's loader, same addon, different defect.

## Decision Record impact

`none` — a consumer calls the wrong accessor.
